steps.name: Import, QC and count preprocessing
caveats: The record does not state whether Salmon gene-level counts are length-corrected; treat them as raw counts for DESeq2 modeling and state this assumption in the output
steps.question: Are the 12,000 gene-level Salmon counts and 120-sample metadata internally consistent for the 60 case vs 60 control design, and which genes are expressed enough to enter the downstream models?
steps.description: Load the Salmon gene-level counts and metadata, verify sample/condition alignment, apply a minimal expression filter, and produce QC diagnostics (library sizes, PCA) on variance-stabilized values. Output: filtered count matrix and VST/logCPM matrix for downstream steps.
acceptance_criteria: Sample IDs of counts.csv (120 samples, 12000 gene rows) and metadata.csv (120 rows) match one-to-one; any mismatch is reported, not silently dropped
Condition balance verified as 60 cases vs 60 controls from the actual metadata values
Low-count filter applied (e.g., keep genes with count >= 10 in at least 10 samples); gene counts before/after reported
Library-size distribution and variance-stabilized/logCPM PCA colored by condition produced; samples flagged as outliers by within-group distance are documented, none removed without justification

steps.name: Case vs control differential expression
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between the 60 cases and 60 controls?
steps.description: Standard DESeq2 differential expression for the unpaired case-control design, with LFC shrinkage and BH correction. The DE table characterizes the biological signal; it must not be used as the classifier feature list (that selection is repeated inside cross-validation in T2S1 to avoid label leakage).
acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 run with design ~ condition on the filtered raw counts; full results table (baseMean, log2FC, Wald stat, p-value, BH padj) written to disk
Number of significant genes reported at FDR < 0.05 and < 0.10
A ranked list by Wald statistic saved for downstream pathway analysis
Volcano and MA plots produced

steps.name: Pathway interpretation of DE genes
caveats: biomaRt requires network access and is unavailable; use the offline org.Hs.eg.db mapping
steps.question: Which WikiPathways human pathways are enriched among the case-vs-control DE genes, and is the DE signal biologically coherent?
steps.description: ORA and pre-ranked GSEA against the WikiPathways human gene sets (HGNC symbols) available in the reference store, mapping gene identifiers via org.Hs.eg.db if the count matrix uses Ensembl/Entrez IDs. This step annotates the DE result; the classifier does not depend on it.
acceptance_criteria: Over-representation analysis on significant DE genes and pre-ranked GSEA (fgsea) on the Wald-statistic-ranked list against the WikiPathways human gene sets
Gene identifier to HGNC symbol mapping coverage reported (skip mapping if the count matrix already uses HGNC symbols); if coverage < 80%, state it explicitly
Ranked enriched-pathway table with NES/p-values written; a clear 'pathway resource absent' report instead of fabricated results if the gene sets are missing

steps.name: Nested-CV benchmark of four classifiers
caveats: DE-gene-derived feature lists are label-informed feature selection on the same samples; using them directly would inflate accuracy — selection must be redone per fold
12000 features vs 120 samples means most models will default to heavy regularization; that is expected and is part of what the CV estimates
steps.question: How accurately can a case-vs-control classifier built on the expressed-gene matrix be expected to perform on a new sample, and does that accuracy exceed chance?
steps.description: Leakage-free accuracy estimation: repeated nested stratified cross-validation of four classifiers on the filtered, normalized expression matrix (VST or logCPM) from T1S1. All feature selection (univariate filter or embedded selection) and hyperparameter tuning happen inside the inner folds, computed only on each outer training split; outer folds are never touched until scoring. Because n=120 with a 12000-gene predictor space, report CIs and a permutation null rather than a point accuracy.
acceptance_criteria: Outer evaluation is repeated stratified 10-fold cross-validation (>= 5 repeats, fixed seed); within every outer training split, hyperparameters AND the feature set are re-selected by inner 5-fold CV from the full filtered gene matrix — the T1S2 DE gene list must NOT be used as features
Four models compared: elastic-net logistic regression (glmnet), random forest (ranger), SVM-RBF (kernlab or e1071), XGBoost
Outer-fold metrics reported per model: AUC, balanced accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, with 95% CIs; a model-comparison table written
Label-permutation null (>= 100 shuffles) on the best model's outer AUC reported as an empirical p-value
Outer-CV (honest) performance reported separately from resubstitution/in-sample performance; the honest number is the headline

steps.name: Final signature and scoring rule
caveats: No independent external cohort is available in this environment (GEO holds no directly comparable downloadable whole-blood case-control set, and the sandbox has no network); the nested-CV estimate is the only accuracy number until a user-supplied validation cohort is provided
steps.question: What is the final case-vs-control gene signature from the 120-sample cohort, and how should a new sample be scored and classified?
steps.description: Refit the winning classifier on all 120 samples with the hyperparameters chosen in T2S1, extract the gene signature, quantify selection stability across outer folds, and package a transparent scoring rule for new samples. The all-sample fit defines the signature; its performance estimate must come from the nested-CV step, not from refitting.
acceptance_criteria: Best model selected by outer-CV performance from T2S1 and refit on all 120 samples with the CV-chosen hyperparameters
Signature table written: selected genes with coefficients/feature importances and effect direction
Feature-selection stability reported: how often each gene is selected across the outer folds of T2S1
A compact top-N signature (most frequently selected genes) presented with its cross-validated performance from T2S1 — never with its all-sample refit performance
Calibration of the final model shown (calibration curve or Brier score); output states explicitly that the all-120-sample fit is optimistic and the quoted accuracy is the nested-CV estimate
Deliverable includes a concrete scoring rule: expression values per gene, direction, and decision threshold

plan.title: Whole-blood case vs control classifier with honest CV accuracy
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a single-batch, unpaired human whole-blood cohort (60 cases vs 60 controls) with gene-level Salmon counts for 12,000 genes over 120 samples. The question — can expression classify case vs control and how accurate would it be on a new sample — is fundamentally an out-of-sample generalization question, so the plan is built around leakage-free accuracy estimation rather than in-sample fit. Flow: (1) import and QC the counts against the 120-row metadata, verify the 60/60 balance, filter near-zero genes, and screen for outliers on a variance-stabilized PCA; (2) run a standard DESeq2 case-vs-control differential expression analysis on the raw counts to characterize the biological signal (this informs interpretation but is explicitly NOT used as the classifier's feature list, because a DE selection done on all 120 samples would leak labels into the feature set); (3) map DE biology to WikiPathways human pathways for interpretability; (4) benchmark four classifiers (elastic-net logistic, random forest, SVM-RBF, XGBoost) under repeated nested stratified cross-validation, where feature selection and hyperparameter tuning happen inside the inner folds on the full filtered expression matrix, and report outer-fold AUC/balanced accuracy/sensitivity/specificity with CIs plus a label-permutation null; (5) refit the best model on all 120 samples to deliver a concrete gene signature and scoring rule, quoting only the cross-validated performance as the accuracy estimate. A GEO search found no directly comparable downloadable whole-blood case-control cohort to validate against, and the sandbox has no network, so external validation is noted as requiring a user-supplied cohort rather than planned as a step.
